style: Calm nurse-style educational guide; synthetic narration

clips.text: The thoracic wall supports breathing and protects the organs beneath it. Begin at the manubrium, follow the body of the sternum and find its xiphoid process. Compare the first ribs with the lower ribs. Costal cartilage connects the anterior rib ends to the sternum in different patterns. Intercostal nerves and vessels need special attention when opening the chest wall. The removable model is a teaching aid; it does not represent a clinical incision plan.
Build a map of ribs, sternum and the protective thoracic cage.

The right lung has three lobes and the left lung has two. Visceral pleura covers the lung; parietal pleura lines the thoracic cavity. The pleural space is normally a potential space between those surfaces. The diaphragm forms the floor of the thorax. Keep anatomical left and right anchored to the specimen, not your screen.

Air passes from the trachea into the right and left main bronchi and then into branching airways. Trace each route in three dimensions. Airway narrowing can limit airflow without a large visible change to the outside of a lung. Close-up teaching views enlarge small structures and should not be mistaken for their life-size dimensions.

The coronary arteries supply the heart muscle. The left and right coronary arteries arise near the root of the aorta. Coronary veins return blood through routes including the coronary sinus. Distinguish a vessel carrying blood to the myocardium from a cardiac chamber containing blood. Cavity reference regions in this collection represent spaces, not pieces of myocardium.

The ascending aorta continues into the aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta. The pulmonary trunk divides toward the lungs. Pulmonary veins return toward the left atrium. Valve leaflets open and close in response to pressure differences. Their arrangement matters as much as their names. Separate components are enlarged or isolated only for teaching.

Air separates the right lung from its chest wall. Review the chest X-ray and the agreed drainage site. Work through a small-bore, wire-guided drain sequence on the enlarged chest-wall model. Its skin, rib, intercostal bundle, pleural space and lung show what each instrument must preserve.
A breathless adult has a right pneumothorax. The case team has selected a small-bore chest drain. One coached step and one needed instrument are shown at a time.
Find the collapsed lung. Point to the right superior lobe. Compare its size with the opposite lung.
Explain the anatomical mechanism. Inspect the specimen and three cutaways. Grip the mechanism that explains this case and release it into the patient-plan dock.
Check the patient and plan. The chest image and indication are already established. Touch the chart with the assessment pointer. Check identity, consent, allergies and the agreed treatment.
Check the planned intercostal space. Locate the upper edge of the lower rib on the cross-section. Avoid the bundle beneath the rib above.
Prepare a sterile field. Move the swab onto the marked skin window. Hold the trigger to clean it; the sterile drape opens.

1. Get comfortable. Welcome to Anatome. I will guide you through the lab. Put on your headset and pick up both controllers. Look for the controller models and pointing rays. Open Menu, then Settings to choose seated or standing comfort and your dominant hand.

This guide stays available from the Guide button. Close guide returns you to the same screen. Your current activity waits while this guide is open.

2. Point and select. Point a controller ray at a button. Squeeze the index trigger to activate a button immediately. Release it before pressing another button. Use the thumbstick while pointing at the panel to scroll. Hold the trigger on a slider and move the ray to adjust it.

Grip the top edge to move the panel. Menu also has Move panel in front of me. Release your controls before returning from a tracking interruption.

3. Hold, move and release. Point at a movable structure or tool. Hold the side grip, move your hand, and turn your wrist. Release the grip to let go. A pointing trigger and a holding grip do different jobs.

Choose Try your first VR lesson, then Learn the VR controls. Select the skin, hold it, lift it, and release. Complete these physical actions to unlock Easy activities. Reading this guide does not complete them.

4. Choose your activity. Choose an activity, a unit, and a difficulty. Learn step by step introduces each action. Practice lets you rehearse. Assessment checks independent performance.

Follow the current step beside the specimen. In lessons and practice, Show me this step provides a demonstration. The Guide button explains controls without revealing assessment answers.

5. Identify and enumerate. Read the requested anatomical name. Inspect the three dimensional specimen, point at the structure, then squeeze and release the trigger. Mark each required structure in the set.

Use the specimen's own left and right. Coverings may be opened as a labelled teaching window. Hidden tissue is not missing anatomy; check the current activity and visible layers.

6. Assemble anatomy. Grip the offered anatomical piece. Easy, lessons and practice show a placement outline. Move the piece into position, turn your wrist to match its orientation, then release. Medium and Hard assessments omit the outline; reconstruct the relationship from surrounding anatomy. Easy introduces one piece at a time.

More demanding levels require closer alignment. If it does not fit, compare the surrounding structures and try again. There is no compulsory countdown.

7. Cut and lift tissue sections. Each topic has its own prepared anatomy stations. Easy, Medium and Hard cover the same anatomy, with less guidance and stricter removal requirements.

Point at the named tissue, hold trigger and sweep a short cut, then release. Grip the separated chunk, lift clear and release. The remaining tissue stays anchored. Follow the removal meter and complete both sides where named.

The bone saw equips automatically for ribs. Saw and scalpel buttons are above the instruction. Both tools reach the first surface within three metres. Losing the surface or pausing cancels the stroke until a fresh press. Preserve protected structures. Undo affects uncollected cuts; completed steps are saved.

8. Work through a case. Inspect the anatomical finding. For a mechanism or response question, grip a three dimensional model and release it inside the patient-plan dock. Read the feedback and reconsider the anatomical relationship.

For a procedure step, choose the indicated equipment, grip it, and use the trigger while completing its target, path or hold. Follow the case one step at a time. These fixed educational scenarios do not establish clinical competence.

9. Finish, review and save. After the required steps, choose Finish activity or Finish assessment. Review the feedback and retry when you need more practice. Pass an assessment with at least eighty percent, every essential objective, and no critical safety failure.

Pass Easy to open Medium, then Medium to open Hard in that activity. Rewards record new unassisted mastery. Sign in to save progress; guest progress lasts only for this session.

10. Adjust or get help. Menu, then Settings provides narration volume and speed, captions, text size and comfort controls. Pause or replay this guide's voice below. Close guide whenever you are ready, and open Guide again to continue here.

If a controller or ray disappears, check tracking and the controller battery, then release trigger and grip before trying again. Recenter the panel from Menu. If a problem persists, stop the activity and record the build version and step for your instructor.

This is a thorax teaching specimen with attributed reconstructions and reference regions. It does not contain the entire human body or every microscopic subdivision.
